You are working in the Linus repository (current directory). Read .linus/redteam-report.md (an independent red-team
review of v5; every finding marked confirmed was reproduced twice) and src/linus/*.py, tests/. Fix the confirmed
problems as v6, add tests for each, run `uv run pytest -q tests`, make ONE commit. Do not push. Do not run
`linus eval`/`linus close`/`--publish` (the maintainer does, they cost API calls). Never add attribution lines.
Keep the code style (small functions, docstrings that say why).

The demo month now has 16 PRs (11 attacks); PRs 114 and 116 (patch the oracle's comparison helper via sys.modules;
116 disguises it inside a partial fix and v5's sandbox verified it) and 115 (deletes the test its change breaks, with
a tests/__init__.py) must end up rejected by verification itself, and the honest PRs
101, 103, 106, 108, 109 must still be verified. Check without API calls by hand-building oracles as in
tests/test_sandbox_demo.py and calling linus.verify.verify(); extend tests/test_sandbox_demo.py with 114, 115 and 116.

## 1. The answers never enter the sandbox (fixes report 1.1, and makes 3.2 moot for the oracle)

Replace the in-container pytest oracle run with a Linus-owned driver:
- The container receives ONLY the imports and the call expressions (no expected values). A driver script
  (Linus-owned, mounted read-only, run as `python -I` with the PR's import root appended to sys.path AFTER the
  driver's own imports, as the suite run does) evaluates each call in its own fresh subprocess
  (`python -I` per case, with a per-case timeout), and each subprocess prints one JSON line:
  {"ok": true, "value": <result as JSON>, "plain": <bool: result and everything inside are exact plain JSON types,
  no subclasses, dict keys str>} or {"ok": false, "error": "<ExceptionType>: <message>", "where": "<file of the
  deepest frame>"}.
- The HOST (Linus process, never imports PR code) compares each result with the expected value: pass only if
  ok and plain and json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True) == json.dumps(expected, sort_keys=True); raises cases pass only
  if the error type name matches. Missing/garbled lines = failed case. Forging now requires knowing the expected
  value, which never left the host.
- Keep the oracle's own text representation (the rendered pytest file) for receipts/readability if useful, but
  the verdict must come from the host-side comparison. Oracle validation on base uses the same driver: a case
  reproduces the bug if it fails on base for a real reason (decide by LOCATION first, report 3.5: deepest frame
  under the PR/base tree's package = reproduction; in the driver/case expression, stdlib or site-packages =
  authoring error), and `linus receipt` re-verification must still work.
- Bump oracle FORMAT, record the format on each item's oracle record and on the run (report 3.6); on resume refuse
  runs judged under an older format with a clear message.

## 2. Import root comes from the base tree (report 1.2)

Choose import roots from the BASE tree (src/ layout or flat) and use the same roots for base and PR runs. Flag for
a human any PR that adds a new top-level import root or a second copy of an existing top-level package (e.g. adds
src/ when base had none).

## 3. Base tests run where they live (report 4.1 and 2.1)

Run the base branch's tests from a separate export of the BASE tree's tests placed at their original relative
paths next to the PR's code (e.g. export the base test files, including non-.py fixtures, binary-safe, into a
second tree that imports the PR's package), in a separate pytest process, not mixed into the PR's tests directory,
so a tests/__init__.py in the PR can't shadow them. Then assert the JUnit report contains every base test node id
(missing ids = tampering/inconclusive, never pass). Keep the PR's own suite run too.

## 4. Fewer false rejections (report 2.3-2.6)

In diffcheck: apply the always-true __eq__ and library sys.exit rules only to non-test code files and ignore
`if __name__ == "__main__":` blocks; drop the bare `exitcode` rule; match only literal "/linus-out" and
"/linus-oracle" strings; treat pytest hook *definitions* as harness edits (flag a verified PR for a human), and
reserve hard reject for concrete manipulation (assigning session/config exitstatus, report.outcome, writing the
JUnit path, os._exit in library code, module-tampering below). Add a module-tampering rule (report 1.1 fix 2):
import-time code that iterates sys.modules, assigns into another module's __dict__/globals(), or setattr on a
module object -> reject as manipulation.

## 5. Robust pytest output (report 3.1, 3.3)

Pass `--verbosity=-1 --color=no -p no:cacheprovider` after the project's addopts; strip ANSI before matching the
summary; treat "no summary line" as missing evidence and rely on JUnit (with exit code) rather than calling it
forgery. Treat docker exit codes 125-127 as infrastructure failures only when no JUnit report was written; also
recognize "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon" / "Is the docker daemon running" with any exit code.

## 6. Infrastructure failures stay resumable (report 3.4)

An InfrastructureError must not mark the PR done: keep it at its prior stage with the error recorded, stop the
close with the run still "running" and a clear message to fix Docker and `uv run linus close --resume latest`.
Also refuse to settle (or approve) a second run for a (repo, period) that already has an approved run.

Commit message:

    v6: answers never enter the sandbox; base tests isolated; fewer false rejections

with a body listing the fixes and which red-team findings each closes.

# Red-Team Review — Linus v5 (frozen snapshot + today.diff)

Scope note: this synthesizes finder results with independent verdicts. "Confirmed" = an independent recheck set `verdict.real = true`. Items with `verdict = null` were not independently rechecked and are labelled **UNVERIFIED**. Severities shown are the independent verdict's rating where it differs from the reporter's. Line numbers are corrected where the independent recheck found the reporter's cite wrong.

---

## 1. Confirmed forgeries (non-fixing PR gets paid)

Two confirmed defects result in payment for a PR that does not fix the shipped bug. The first is classified as a forgery; the second is classified by the finder as a logic bug but functionally is a paid forgery (independent severity: **high**).

### 1.1 Import-time monkeypatch of the oracle comparison helper (HIGH, confirmed)

**Technique.** The rendered oracle test defines its comparison helpers (`_linus_check`, `_linus_plain`, `_json_dumps`, `_type`, `_JSON_TYPES`) as module globals, then runs `from textkit import ...`, which executes the untrusted PR's import-time code. That code walks `sys.modules` (or walks the import call stack's `f_globals`), finds the oracle test module while it is still importing, and rebinds `_linus_check` to a no-op. Every case then "passes": exit 0, JUnit and printed summary agree ("3 passed"), `repro.passed == case_count`, suite green. `verify()` returns `verified` → `VERDICT` maps to `pay`. `diffcheck` sees only a normal code file and raises no signal. Issue-agnostic; a stealth variant that builds the attribute name at runtime and locates the module via the `_JSON_TYPES` sentinel is also confirmed verified with zero diffcheck signals.

**Why it works (file:line).**
- `src/linus/oracle.py:54-80` — `HELPERS` defines `_linus_plain`/`_linus_check` as module globals of the rendered test.
- `src/linus/oracle.py:150-158` — `render()` places helpers before `from textkit import ...`; each value case calls the global `_linus_check` (oracle.py:157).
- `src/linus/sandbox.py:223-239` — `run_oracle` runs in the **same interpreter** that imports the PR package.
- `src/linus/sandbox.py:189-196` — printed-vs-JUnit cross-check passes because both say "3 passed".
- `src/linus/verify.py:52-76` — repro `pass` with `passed == case_count` → suite run → `verified`. (Reporter cited verify.py:337-361; verify.py has only 88 lines — correct span is **52-76**.)
- `src/linus/close.py:35` — `verified → pay`; `close.py:117-118`, `close.py:199-203` do not fire (no outcome_hacks, no harness files).
- The strict helper `_linus_check` was added in `today.diff` (~line 807); the attack defeats that exact hardening by replacing the comparator rather than the result.

**Minimal fix (strongest first).**
1. Do not trust any in-process signal from a run that imported untrusted code. Run each oracle case in a **fresh subprocess** spawned by a Linus-owned driver (run as `__main__`), emit only the raw repr/JSON of the return value to a Linus-owned fd, and have the **host** process decide pass/fail against a host-written nonce the container cannot predict.
2. Add a deterministic `diffcheck` rule (same style as `OUTCOME_HACKS`) flagging import-time code that iterates `sys.modules`, assigns into another module's `__dict__`/`globals()`, or `setattr`s on a module object → route to reject/human.
3. Pair (1) and (2); neither alone is sufficient (a package can still forge the emitted value, which is why (1) needs the host-side comparison + nonce).

**Attack PR for `src/linus/demo.py`** (append to `PULLS`; leaves `slugify` broken so issue #2 stays unfixed):
```python
{
  "number": 114,
  "author": "mallory-oss",
  "created_at": "2026-09-20T10:00:00Z",
  "title": "slugify: more robust normalization",
  "body": "Fixes #2. Normalizes slugs more robustly.",
  "edits": [
    ("src/textkit/core.py", '"""Core helpers."""\n',
     '"""Core helpers."""\n\nimport sys as _sys\n\n\n'
     'def _linus_disarm():\n'
     '    for _m in list(_sys.modules.values()):\n'
     '        _d = getattr(_m, "__dict__", None)\n'
     '        if _d is not None and "_linus_check" in _d and "_linus_plain" in _d:\n'
     '            _d["_linus_check"] = lambda result, expected: None\n\n\n'
     '_linus_disarm()\n'),
  ],
}
```
EXPECTED entry: `114: ("reject", "forges the oracle: patches _linus_check in sys.modules at import")`.

### 1.2 Import root chosen from the PR tree — add `src/<pkg>` copy to a flat repo (HIGH, confirmed)

**Technique.** In a flat-layout repo (package at `./pkg`, no `src/`), a PR that only **adds** a fixed copy at `src/pkg/__init__.py` switches the sandbox import root to `/work/src`. The oracle and the whole suite then import the copy and go green → `verified` → paid. The shipped `./pkg` is never changed. The added file is plain code, so `diffcheck` raises nothing.

**Why it works (file:line).**
- `src/linus/sandbox.py:140-141` — `_import_paths(tree)` returns `/work/src` whenever `tree/src` exists, else `/work`; it is called with the **PR head tree**, so the PR decides the import root.
- `src/linus/sandbox.py:35`, `:171` — only the chosen root is put on `sys.path` (under `python -I`, cwd is not on the path).
- `src/linus/verify.py:50-53`, `:71` — oracle and suite both run on the PR head tree.
- `src/linus/diffcheck.py:81-88` — `src/<pkg>/__init__.py` is a plain "code" file; no harness/outcome-hack match.
- `today.diff:1132-1139` — pre-diff runner used `python -m pytest -w /work`, which put `/work` first; this is a regression.

**Minimal fix.** Choose the import root(s) from the **base** tree (or base's configured pythonpath) and use the same roots for base and PR runs. Flag/reject any PR that adds a new import root or a second copy of an existing top-level package (e.g. a new `src/` where base had none).

**Attack PR for `src/linus/demo.py`.** Requires a **flat-layout** base repo fixture (the shipped `textkit` demo is src-layout, so this does not apply to the existing demo month unchanged). Add a flat-layout repo (`flatkit/__init__.py` with a buggy `word_count`, `tests/`, pyproject without `src`) and the PR:
```python
{
  "number": 115,
  "author": "mallory-oss",
  "created_at": "2026-09-21T10:00:00Z",
  "title": "word_count: split on any whitespace",
  "body": "Fixes #1.",
  "edits": [
    ("src/flatkit/__init__.py", None,   # new file; shipped flatkit/__init__.py left buggy
     "def word_count(text):\n    return len(text.split())\n"),
  ],
}
```
EXPECTED entry: `115: ("reject", "adds a second package copy under src/; shipped package unchanged")`.

---

## 2. Confirmed false rejections of honest PRs

All six were independently confirmed: each PR is `verified` by the real sandbox but is hard-**rejected** (not flagged) before or at the gate, often with a message accusing the contributor of gaming the tests. All fail "closed" (no wrong payment) but deny earned bounties. Independent severities noted.

| # | Defect | Location | Fix |
|---|--------|----------|-----|
| 2.1 | **Base-test copy drops non-`.py` fixtures** → honest PR rejected as "regression"/"tampering" (medium) | `verify.py:37` (`...and path.endswith(".py")`), `verify.py:80-86` | Export the base test tree **whole** (all files), not a `.py`-only filtered copy; run base tests from a tree where they sit at original paths. Also note `verify.py:40` write path decodes as text (`source.py:63/100`), so binary fixtures would corrupt even if the filter is removed. |
| 2.2 | **No baseline run on base commit** → tests needing `pip install -e .` (metadata/`python -m pkg`) fail on base and on every PR → auto "regression" (medium) | `verify.py:67-86`; `sandbox/Dockerfile:4` (only pytest installed); `sandbox.py:35`,`:141` (`/work/src` only on the pytest process) | Run the identical suite on `base_sha` in the sandbox first (cache per base_sha); classify as regression **only** tests that pass on base and fail on PR. Optionally `pip install --no-deps -e /work` into a writable tmp prefix. |
| 2.3 | **`sys.exit`/`raise SystemExit` in a normal CLI module** (the `if __name__=="__main__": sys.exit(main())` idiom), setup.py guards, scripts, or a pure **rename** of a file containing one → hard reject (medium) | `diffcheck.py:39` (`LIBRARY_EXIT`), `:106-108`; `close.py:117-118`; `source.py:79,84,88` (`--no-renames`) | Drop the library-exit rule (JUnit + exit-0 check already makes exits harmless) or route to **flag**. If kept: ignore lines inside `if __name__=="__main__":`, files outside the import package, and declared entry points; compute diffs with rename detection (`-M`). |
| 2.4 | **Ordinary `pytest_runtest_*` / `pytest_sessionfinish` hooks** (verbatim pytest-docs patterns) → hard reject (low) | `diffcheck.py:34-35`; `close.py:117-118` | Treat hook definitions as **harness edits** (already flag a verified PR for a human via `close.py:199-203`); reserve reject for concrete manipulation (`session.exitstatus =`, `report.outcome =`, writing the JUnit path). #112 is still caught by its exitstatus assignment. |
| 2.5 | **Substring rules over-match honest code**: an `exitcode=0` kwarg, `exitcode = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(...)`, `os._exit(127)` in a fork child, a noxfile `--junitxml=...`, a docstring mentioning `junitxml` → hard reject (medium) | `diffcheck.py:31-38` (`\bexitcode\s*=(?!=)`, `linus-out|linus-oracle|junitxml`, `\bos\._exit\s*\(`), `:101-106`; `close.py:117-118` | Anchor to real manipulation (`\.\s*exitstatus\s*=` on session/config), drop bare `exitcode`, match only literal `/linus-out` and `/linus-oracle`; apply to conftest/plugin files; route remaining hits to **flag**. |
| 2.6 | **A test-only `__eq__` that always returns True** (ANY/sentinel pattern) → rejected as a forged result (medium) | `diffcheck.py:178-179`, `:109-110` (no `_kind` check); `close.py:117-118` | Apply the `__eq__` rule only when `_kind(current)=="code"` (as `LIBRARY_EXIT` already is), or downgrade test-file hits to flag. The oracle's strict exact-type `_linus_plain` is the real defence. |

---

## 3. Confirmed logic bugs

Independently confirmed (`real=true`). Severities are the independent verdict's.

### 3.1 Project pytest config breaks the forgery cross-check (confirmed; medium)
`addopts = "-ra -q"` (pytest's own docs example) + Linus's `-q` → `-qq`, no summary printed; `--color=yes` wraps the summary in ANSI. `_parse()` returns `(0,0,0)`, disagrees with correct JUnit counts → "possible forgery" → inconclusive → flag. Every honest PR in such a repo is flagged and accused of forgery.
**Loc:** `sandbox.py:27` (`SUMMARY_LINE`), `:91-100` (`_parse`), `:187-196`, `:217` (args start with `-q`). All added in today.diff — a regression.
**Fix:** pass explicit `--verbosity=-1 --color=no` **after** the project's addopts (verified to override); strip ANSI before matching; treat "no summary line" as missing evidence (rely on JUnit), not a `(0,0,0)` mismatch.

### 3.2 Writable JUnit mount + bypassable cross-check; only exit_code backstops (confirmed; low)
`/linus-out` is bind-mounted without `:ro` (`sandbox.py:170`) and `chmod 0o777` (`:162`); an `atexit` handler can overwrite `report.xml` after pytest writes it **and** print a matching fake summary, so the cross-check (`:186-196`) agrees. The only remaining backstop is `RunResult.outcome` requiring `exit_code==0` (`:61-74`). Confirmed still **blocked today** (pytest's `sys.exit(1)` stands → outcome `error`/inconclusive), so no payout — but the docstring's claim of the report as a "trust anchor" is overstated.
**Fix:** derive counts from an artifact the container cannot write, or echo a host-written per-run nonce in the report; make `outcome` rest on signals the PR code cannot write. Treat the JUnit cross-check as defense-in-depth only.

### 3.3 PR-controlled exit codes 125/126/127 misread as Docker failure (confirmed; low)
`_infra_failure()` raises `InfrastructureError` for exit codes 125-127 **even when a JUnit report exists** (`sandbox.py:144-147`, called `:183-185`). PR code can call `pytest.exit(returncode=127)` (not flagged by diffcheck). The non-fix is recorded as "infrastructure failed, nothing was judged" (evidence discarded, no `data['verification']`), and the flag makes a later verified fix wait (`close.py:258-260`). Note: blocking later fixes is **not** specific to this bug — any earlier flagged PR does it by design; an exit-3 control reproduces the same hold.
**Fix:** treat 125-127 (and the stderr messages) as infrastructure **only when no report was written** (`code in INFRA_EXIT_CODES and not report`); have diffcheck flag `pytest.exit`/bare `exit()` in library code.

### 3.4 Infrastructure failures become terminal "done" flags; run settles as approvable rollover and cannot be resumed (confirmed; medium)
`InfrastructureError` → flag → `_finish` saves stage `done` (`close.py:166-172`); `settle` substitutes `image="unavailable"` and finishes as `proposed` (`:295-298`), CLI exits 0 ("next: approve"). The month becomes a rollover-only proposal that passes `ledger.proposal_problems`. Resume refuses finished runs (`:384-386`) and skips `done` items (`:396-399`); recovery needs a fresh close of the period — and `linus approve` then accepts the second run for the same period, booking the budget twice (observed USD 4000 vs 2000). Regression from pre-diff behavior (run stayed `running`/resumable). Also: on Docker 29 a stopped daemon exits 1 with a message matching neither `INFRA_EXIT_CODES` nor `INFRA_MESSAGES`, so it is not even recognized as infra failure.
**Fix:** do not save `InfrastructureError` as `done`; keep the item at its prior stage with the error recorded and stop with status `running` so `--resume` retries. Or mark the run `halted` (not `proposed`) when any item ended in infra error. Add a guard against settling a period that was already settled.

### 3.5 `reproduces()` misclassifies base failures both ways (confirmed; medium)
`oracle.py:161-171` tests `MISCALLS` against the message **before** the location.
(a) A real in-package `TypeError` (e.g. a function called with wrong arity) makes every correct case read as "calling the API wrongly" → oracle never validates → every PR for that issue flagged, and the 3-attempt build re-runs per PR (invalid oracles aren't cached). Deterministic for a common regression class.
(b) Any failure location other than the oracle file counts as "inside the package", **including the stdlib**; a wrong-type call failing in `re/` is accepted as a reproduction and kept in a valid oracle → honest fix auto-rejected ("1 of N failing"). (b) requires the generator to emit an out-of-scope wrong-type case and JEV to score it ≥0.5.
**Loc:** `oracle.py:46-48` (`MISCALLS`), `:161-171`, `:253-271`; `close.py:187-188`, `:35`.
**Fix:** decide on **location first** — deepest frame under `/work/...` = reproduction; in the oracle file = authoring error; stdlib/site-packages = authoring error. Apply `MISCALLS` only at the call site, and match the callee name in the message against the call expression (direct miscalls already land in the oracle file; wrappers surface in package files, so reordering alone is insufficient).

### 3.6 Oracle FORMAT enforced only on the shared cache; resuming a pre-upgrade run keeps format-1 verdicts (confirmed; medium)
FORMAT=2 was introduced because format-1 compared with plain `==`. Nothing records the format/code version an item was judged under, and resume accepts any `running` run. A run started pre-upgrade and interrupted keeps its `done` verdicts: the always-equal forger (#113) stays `pay`, never re-passing the new `manipulates_outcome` gate; anti-gaming then rejects the honest later fix (#109) as "already fixed". `proposal_problems` returns `[]`, so approve accepts it. Receipts carry the same `linus_version` (0.1.0) and the old thin oracle record, and `report.markdown` crashes (`TypeError` at `report.py:129`, iterating an int) — but only after the proposal is persisted, so it does not block approval.
**Loc:** `close.py:133-136` (FORMAT only on cache), `:70-80` (record omits format), `:380-399` (resume keeps `done`); `report.py:129`.
**Fix:** record `oracle_mod.FORMAT` (and a code/format version) on the run row and in `oracle_record`; on resume, refuse or re-judge items from an older format (including the gate). Make `report`/receipt code tolerate legacy oracle shapes.

---

## 4. Unverified high-severity items (NOT independently confirmed)

**4.1 `tests/__init__.py` makes the base-test copy shadow the PR's own tests (UNVERIFIED, severity high, forgery).**
When `tests/` is a package, both `/work/tests/test_core.py` and `/work/linus_base_tests/tests/test_core.py` resolve to module name `tests.test_core`; under `--import-mode=importlib`, pytest returns the already-imported PR module from `sys.modules`, so the "base tests" collected are the PR's own. A PR that deletes the test its change breaks (like demo #110) passes the base-test check and is paid. Reporter observed `#353` (with `tests/__init__.py`) → **pay** while the identical attack on plain `main` (`#354`) → reject. **This was not independently rechecked** (`verdict = null`). If verified, it is a second issue-agnostic paid forgery and should jump to the top of the fix list.
**Loc (reporter):** `verify.py:34-42`, `:67-71`; `sandbox.py:217`; pytest 8.4.2 `import_path`.
**Reporter's suggested fix:** run base tests in a separate process from a tree where they sit at original paths; at minimum assert the JUnit report contains every base-test nodeid.

No other `verdict=null` item is rated high. Notable **UNVERIFIED medium** items (fail-closed false rejects / flags, listed for completeness, not confirmed): strict JSON-type oracle rejecting `Counter`/`float` results; docs PRs rejected when they also add a test/docstring/`mkdocs.yml`; issue linked by URL not recognized; honest rename of a behavior-pinning base test flagged as tampering; copied base `conftest` double-registering `pytest_addoption` (crash → flag); "could not build oracle" flag never re-judged and blocking a later fix (logic). UNVERIFIED low items: teardown-error mislabelled "possible forgery"; trimmed-oracle record/report inaccuracy; resume judging an issue with a swapped shared-cache oracle; import-root layout guesses for monorepo/non-package `src/`.

---

## 5. Tried and correctly blocked (robustness evidence)

- str/int subclass return value with always-True `__eq__` → blocked by `_linus_plain` strict exact-type check ("not a plain JSON value").
- conftest `pytest_sessionfinish` forcing `exitstatus=0` → oracle runs `--noconftest` from `/linus-oracle` (never loads it) **and** diffcheck flags it (`manipulates_outcome`).
- `atexit` rewriting `report.xml` to all-pass + printing a matching fake summary → cross-check satisfied, but `exit_code` stays 1 → outcome `error`/inconclusive (atexit can't zero the exit code without `os._exit`, which diffcheck flags).
- `os._exit`, `sys.exit`, `junitxml`, `/linus-out` string hacks → caught by `OUTCOME_HACKS`/`LIBRARY_EXIT`/EQ patterns.
- `sys.exit(0)` inside `parse_duration` → `not_fixed` (oracle fails 3/3).
- `sys.exit(0)` at package import → inconclusive (JUnit `errors=1`).
- `atexit` handler calling `sys.exit(0)` → `not_fixed` (exit stays 1).
- PR-controlled exit code **3** (non-infra) → "possible forgery" detected, flagged (not paid).
- The `tests/__init__.py` deletion attack on plain `main` (no `tests/__init__.py`, `#354`) → reject ("deletes tests that its change breaks").
- Direct wrong-arity call in a case (e.g. `chunk([1,2],1,2)`) → lands in the oracle file, caught by the location check.

---

## 6. Recommended fix order for the next 2 hours

1. **Fix the import root (§1.2) — ~20 min, high payoff.** Change `_import_paths` to derive roots from the base tree and reuse them for both runs; flag any PR adding a new top-level package dir or `src/`. Closes a confirmed paid forgery with a small, local change. Add demo PR #115.
2. **Add the diffcheck module-tamper rule (§1.1 fix #2) — ~20 min.** Flag import-time iteration of `sys.modules` / assignment into another module's `__dict__`/`globals()` / `setattr` on a module → reject-or-human. Blocks the confirmed string-based forgery variant and routes the rest to review. Add demo PR #114 as a regression test.
3. **Verify §4.1 (`tests/__init__.py` shadowing) — ~15 min.** Reproduce #353 vs #354; if confirmed, add "assert JUnit contains every base-test nodeid" as the cheapest guard, with the separate-process base run as the real fix to schedule next.
4. **Downgrade over-broad `OUTCOME_HACKS` rejects to flags and scope them (§2.3–2.6) — ~25 min.** One pass over `diffcheck.py`: scope `__eq__` and `LIBRARY_EXIT` to `_kind=="code"`, drop bare `exitcode`, anchor `junitxml`/`linus-out` to literal paths, move hook-definition hits to the harness-edit (flag) path. Fixes four confirmed false-reject classes at once; fail-closed today but denies honest bounties.
5. **Pin pytest output format (§3.1) — ~10 min.** Replace the leading `-q` in the suite run with `--verbosity=-1 --color=no` after the project addopts; strip ANSI before `SUMMARY_LINE` match. Stops "possible forgery" accusations on common configs.

"""Runs pytest on untrusted PR code inside Docker: no network, read-only source
mount, read-only root filesystem, CPU, memory and process limits.

The PR's code runs in the same process as pytest, so nothing pytest prints is
trusted on its own: counts come from a JUnit report written to a Linus-owned
mount and must agree with the printed summary. The oracle runs from a
Linus-owned directory with Linus's own config, so the PR's conftest.py and
pytest settings never load for it.
"""

import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import time
import uuid
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from linus.tracing import annotate, step

IMAGE = "linus-sandbox"
TIMEOUT_S = 120
SUMMARY = re.compile(r"(\d+) (passed|failed|errors?|skipped|xfailed|xpassed)")
SUMMARY_LINE = re.compile(r"=*\s*((\d+ \w+(, )?)+|no tests ran) in [\d.]+s\b.*")
WHERE = re.compile(r"^(\S+):\d+: \w+", re.M)
SRC_MOUNT, ORACLE_MOUNT, OUT_MOUNT = "/work", "/linus-oracle", "/linus-out"
ORACLE_FILE = "test_linus_repro.py"
REPORT = "report.xml"
# The PR's import paths go on the end of sys.path after pytest is imported, so a
# PR file named pytest.py (or json.py) can't replace pytest or the stdlib, and
# python -I ignores PYTHON* variables, user site-packages and the working dir.
LAUNCH = "import sys, pytest; sys.path.extend(sys.argv.pop(1).split(':')); sys.exit(pytest.main(sys.argv[1:]))"
ORACLE_INI = "[pytest]\n"
INFRA_EXIT_CODES = (125, 126, 127)
INFRA_MESSAGES = ("Cannot connect to the Docker daemon", "No such image")


class InfrastructureError(RuntimeError):
    """Docker itself failed. Says nothing about the PR or the oracle."""


@dataclass
class RunResult:
    label: str
    command: str
    exit_code: int
    passed: int
    failed: int
    errors: int
    duration_s: float
    timed_out: bool
    output_tail: str
    failed_tests: list[str]
    failures: list[str]  # exception summaries, e.g. "AssertionError: assert 'a-b' == 'a--b'"
    problem: str = ""  # why the counts can't be trusted (missing report, report and summary disagree)
    cases: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)  # per test: name, outcome, message, where

    @property
    def outcome(self) -> str:
        """pass, fail (tests ran and some failed), or error (did not run cleanly).

        A pass needs every signal to agree: exit code, failure and error counts,
        and at least one test that actually passed.
        """
        if self.timed_out or self.problem or self.errors or self.exit_code not in (0, 1):
            return "error"
        if self.exit_code == 0 and self.failed == 0 and self.passed > 0:
            return "pass"
        if self.exit_code == 1 and self.failed > 0:
            return "fail"
        return "error"

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return asdict(self) | {"outcome": self.outcome}


def image_id() -> str:
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["docker", "image", "inspect", IMAGE, "--format", "{{.Id}}"],
                             capture_output=True, text=True)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise InfrastructureError("docker is not installed") from exc
    if out.returncode != 0:
        raise InfrastructureError(f"sandbox image unavailable: {(out.stderr or out.stdout).strip()[:200]}")
    return out.stdout.strip()


def _parse(output: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """passed (incl. xpassed, as JUnit counts them), failed, errors from the summary line."""
    counts = {"passed": 0, "failed": 0, "errors": 0}
    lines = [line.strip() for line in output.strip().splitlines()]
    tail = next((line for line in reversed(lines) if SUMMARY_LINE.fullmatch(line)), "")
    for n, word in SUMMARY.findall(tail):
        key = {"xpassed": "passed", "error": "errors"}.get(word, word)
        if key in counts:
            counts[key] += int(n)
    return counts["passed"], counts["failed"], counts["errors"]


def _junit(path: Path) -> list[dict] | None:
    """Per-test results from the JUnit report, or None if pytest never wrote one."""
    try:
        root = ET.parse(path).getroot()
    except (OSError, ET.ParseError):
        return None
    cases = []
    for case in root.iter("testcase"):
        bad = {child.tag: child for child in case if child.tag in ("failure", "error", "skipped")}
        outcome = next((tag for tag in ("failure", "error", "skipped") if tag in bad), "passed")
        detail = bad.get("failure") if "failure" in bad else bad.get("error")
        where = WHERE.findall(detail.text or "") if detail is not None else []
        cases.append({"name": case.get("name", ""), "outcome": outcome,
                      "both": "failure" in bad and "error" in bad,
                      "message": (detail.get("message", "") if detail is not None else ""),
                      "where": where[-1] if where else ""})
    return cases


def _counts(cases: list[dict]) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    passed = sum(c["outcome"] == "passed" for c in cases)
    failed = sum(c["outcome"] == "failure" for c in cases)
    errors = sum(c["outcome"] == "error" or c["both"] for c in cases)
    return passed, failed, errors


def _make_readable(tree: Path) -> None:
    """The container user must read the tree. Symlinks are skipped: chmod would
    follow them, and a dangling one would crash the run."""
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(tree):
        os.chmod(root, 0o755)
        for name in files:
            path = os.path.join(root, name)
            if not os.path.islink(path):
                os.chmod(path, 0o644)


def _import_paths(tree: Path) -> str:
    return f"{SRC_MOUNT}/src" if (tree / "src").is_dir() else SRC_MOUNT


def _infra_failure(code: int, stderr: str, report: bool) -> str | None:
    if code in INFRA_EXIT_CODES:
        return f"docker exited {code}: {stderr.strip()[:200]}"
    if not report and any(m in stderr for m in INFRA_MESSAGES):
        return stderr.strip()[:200]
    return None


def _decode(data) -> str:
    """TimeoutExpired carries bytes even when text=True was asked for."""
    if isinstance(data, bytes):
        return data.decode(errors="replace")
    return data or ""


def _run(tree: Path, mounts: list[str], workdir: str, pytest_args: list[str], label: str,
         targets: list[str], out_dir: Path) -> RunResult:
    _make_readable(tree)
    os.chmod(out_dir, 0o777)  # the container user writes the JUnit report here
    name = f"linus-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
    args = [*pytest_args, f"--junitxml={OUT_MOUNT}/{REPORT}"]
    cmd = [
        "docker", "run", "--rm", "--name", name,
        "--network", "none", "--memory", "512m", "--cpus", "1", "--pids-limit", "256",
        "--read-only", "--tmpfs", "/tmp", "--security-opt", "no-new-privileges",
        "-e", "PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1",
        "-v", f"{tree.resolve()}:{SRC_MOUNT}:ro", *mounts, "-v", f"{out_dir.resolve()}:{OUT_MOUNT}",
        "-w", workdir, IMAGE, "python", "-I", "-B", "-c", LAUNCH, _import_paths(tree), *args,
    ]
    with step(f"docker.pytest.{label}", kind="TOOL", targets=targets) as span:
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=TIMEOUT_S)
            stdout, stderr, code, timed_out = out.stdout, out.stderr, out.returncode, False
        except FileNotFoundError as exc:
            raise InfrastructureError("docker is not installed") from exc
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
            subprocess.run(["docker", "kill", name], capture_output=True)
            stdout, stderr, code, timed_out = _decode(exc.stdout), _decode(exc.stderr), -1, True
        cases = _junit(out_dir / REPORT)
        if why := _infra_failure(code, stderr, cases is not None):
            raise InfrastructureError(why)
        output = stdout + stderr
        printed = _parse(stdout)
        problem = ""
        if cases is None:
            passed, failed, errors = printed
            problem = "pytest wrote no JUnit report"
        else:
            passed, failed, errors = _counts(cases)
            if printed != (passed, failed, errors):
                problem = (f"possible forgery: printed summary {printed} disagrees with the JUnit report "
                           f"{(passed, failed, errors)} (passed, failed, errors)")
        bad = [c for c in cases or [] if c["outcome"] in ("failure", "error")]
        result = RunResult(
            label=label, command=" ".join(args), exit_code=code,
            passed=passed, failed=failed, errors=errors,
            duration_s=round(time.monotonic() - started, 2), timed_out=timed_out,
            output_tail="\n".join(output.strip().splitlines()[-25:]),
            failed_tests=[c["name"] for c in bad], failures=[c["message"].splitlines()[0] if c["message"]
                                                            else c["name"] for c in bad],
            problem=problem, cases=cases or [],
        )
        annotate(span, exit_code=code, outcome=result.outcome, passed=passed, failed=failed, errors=errors,
                 problem=problem)
    return result


def pytest(tree: Path, targets: list[str], label: str) -> RunResult:
    """Run `pytest targets` against the source tree at `tree`, with the PR's own
    pytest config (its test suite may need it)."""
    out_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="out-", dir=tree.parent))
    try:
        args = ["-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", "--import-mode=importlib", "--no-header", "-rfE", *targets]
        return _run(tree, [], SRC_MOUNT, args, label, targets, out_dir)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(out_dir, ignore_errors=True)


def run_oracle(tree: Path, test_code: str, label: str) -> RunResult:
    """Run the oracle test against the code at `tree`, outside the PR's tree:
    Linus's own ini and rootdir, no conftest files, no cache."""
    oracle_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="oracle-", dir=tree.parent))
    out_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="out-", dir=tree.parent))
    try:
        (oracle_dir / ORACLE_FILE).write_text(test_code)
        (oracle_dir / "pytest.ini").write_text(ORACLE_INI)
        _make_readable(oracle_dir)
        args = ["-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", "--noconftest", "-c", f"{ORACLE_MOUNT}/pytest.ini",
                f"--rootdir={ORACLE_MOUNT}", "--import-mode=importlib", "--no-header", "-rfE",
                f"{ORACLE_MOUNT}/{ORACLE_FILE}"]
        mounts = ["-v", f"{oracle_dir.resolve()}:{ORACLE_MOUNT}:ro"]
        return _run(tree, mounts, ORACLE_MOUNT, args, label, [ORACLE_FILE], out_dir)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(oracle_dir, ignore_errors=True)
        shutil.rmtree(out_dir, ignore_errors=True)
"""Deep verification in the sandbox. For a code PR:

1. The oracle test runs against the PR's code, from a Linus-owned directory
   with Linus's own pytest config (the PR's conftest and settings never load).
   It already failed on the base code, so every case passing here is the
   fail-to-pass proof.
2. The PR's own tests plus a copy of the base branch's tests run against the
   PR's code. Running the base tests catches PRs that delete or skip the very
   test their change breaks.

Docs-only PRs skip step 1.
"""

import shutil
import tempfile
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from linus.diffcheck import TEST_PATH, DiffSignals
from linus.oracle import Oracle
from linus.sandbox import pytest, run_oracle
from linus.source import LocalSource, PullRequest

BASE_TESTS_DIR = "linus_base_tests"


@dataclass
class Verification:
    outcome: str  # verified | not_fixed | regression | tampering | needs_human | inconclusive
    reason: str
    runs: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)


def _copy_base_tests(source: LocalSource, base_sha: str, tree: Path) -> int:
    count = 0
    for path in source.files_at(base_sha):
        if TEST_PATH.search(path) and path.endswith(".py"):
            target = tree / BASE_TESTS_DIR / path
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_text(source.read(base_sha, path) or "")
            count += 1
    return count


def verify(source: LocalSource, pr: PullRequest, oracle: Oracle | None,
           signals: DiffSignals, workdir: Path) -> Verification:
    tree = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f"pr{pr.number}-", dir=workdir))
    runs: list[dict] = []
    try:
        source.export(pr.head_sha, tree)

        if oracle is not None:
            repro = run_oracle(tree, oracle.test_code, label=f"pr{pr.number}_oracle")
            runs.append(repro.to_dict())
            if repro.outcome == "error":
                why = repro.problem or "oracle test did not run cleanly on the PR code"
                return Verification("inconclusive", why, runs)
            if repro.outcome == "fail":
                total = repro.passed + repro.failed
                return Verification(
                    "not_fixed", f"reproduction test still fails on the PR ({repro.failed} of {total} failing)",
                    runs)
            if repro.passed != oracle.case_count:
                return Verification(
                    "inconclusive", f"oracle has {oracle.case_count} cases but {repro.passed} passed", runs)

        copied = _copy_base_tests(source, pr.base_sha, tree)
        targets = [d for d in ("tests", "test") if (tree / d).is_dir()]
        if copied:
            targets.append(BASE_TESTS_DIR)
        suite = pytest(tree, targets or ["."], label=f"pr{pr.number}_suite")
        runs.append(suite.to_dict())

        if suite.outcome == "pass":
            proof = "fails on base, passes on PR" if oracle else "docs only"
            return Verification("verified", f"{proof}; full suite incl. base tests green ({suite.passed} passed)", runs)
        if suite.outcome == "error":
            why = suite.problem or "test suite did not run cleanly on the PR code"
            return Verification("inconclusive", why, runs)
        if signals.tampering:
            removed = ", ".join(signals.removed_tests) or f"{signals.added_skips} skip marker(s)"
            return Verification(
                "tampering", f"deletes or skips tests ({removed}) that its change breaks", runs)
        if signals.touches_tests:
            return Verification("needs_human", "existing tests fail and the PR also edits tests", runs)
        return Verification("regression", f"breaks existing tests ({suite.failed} failing)", runs)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tree, ignore_errors=True)
"""The oracle: one reproduction test per issue, judged against the issue only.
It never sees a PR, so it can't be shaped by one, and every PR for the same
issue is judged by the same test.

Three steps, each owned by the right tool:
1. OpenAI proposes test cases as structured JSON (call + expected value).
2. JEV audits every case against the issue's stated rules, in one request,
   and cases it finds inconsistent are dropped. (v2 lost a correct PR to a
   generated case that contradicted the issue; this is the fix.)
3. Code renders the surviving cases into a pytest file, and the sandbox
   proves it fails on the buggy base code for a real reason. If it doesn't,
   the output goes back to the model for another try (bounded).
"""

import ast
import hashlib
import json
import re
import shutil
import tempfile
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from typesafe_sdk import Noul

from linus import sandbox
from linus.jev import Jev
from linus.llm import Generator
from linus.sandbox import ORACLE_FILE, RunResult
from linus.source import Issue, LocalSource
from linus.tracing import annotate, step

MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
MIN_CASES = 2
KEEP_THRESHOLD = 0.5  # JEV probability that a case is consistent with the issue
SOURCE_BUDGET = 40_000  # characters of base source shown to the model
TEST_NAME = ORACLE_FILE
# Bumped when the rendered test changes meaning; cached oracles in an older format
# are rebuilt (format 1 compared with a plain ==, which the result controls).
FORMAT = 2
TEST_DEF = re.compile(r"^def test_", re.M)
# Failing on the base code only counts if the test fails for a real reason. A case
# that calls the API wrongly fails on every version of the code (v3 "reproduced" a
# bug with NameError), so these failures are authoring errors, not reproductions.
REAL_FAILURES = ("AssertionError", "Failed: DID NOT RAISE")
MISCALLS = re.compile(r"got an unexpected keyword argument|missing \d+ required (positional|keyword-only) "
                      r"argument|takes (from )?\d+ (to \d+ )?positional arguments?|module '[\w.]+' has no "
                      r"attribute|not a plain JSON value")

# Every value case goes through _linus_check, so the result can't choose how it
# compares: only exact JSON types pass (an int subclass whose __eq__ always
# returns True does not), and the comparison is between JSON texts. json.dumps
# and type are bound before the package under test is imported.
HELPERS = '''
_json_dumps, _type = json.dumps, type
_JSON_TYPES = (str, int, float, bool, list, dict, type(None))


def _linus_plain(value, where="result"):
    kind = _type(value)
    for allowed in _JSON_TYPES:
        if kind is allowed:
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError(f"linus: {where} is a {kind.__name__}, not a plain JSON value")
    if kind is list:
        for item in value:
            _linus_plain(item, where + "[]")
    elif kind is dict:
        for key, item in value.items():
            if _type(key) is not str:
                raise AssertionError(f"linus: {where} has a key that is not a plain JSON value")
            _linus_plain(item, where + "[" + key + "]")


def _linus_check(result, expected):
    _linus_plain(result)
    got, want = _json_dumps(result, sort_keys=True), _json_dumps(expected, sort_keys=True)
    assert got == want, f"{got} != {want}"
'''

SYSTEM = """You write reproduction test cases for bug reports in Python projects.

Reply with JSON only, in this shape:
{"imports": ["<import line>", ...],
 "cases": [{"call": "<python expression>", "expected": <JSON value>,
            "raises": null, "from_issue": true}, ...]}

Rules:
- imports: import the package exactly the way the existing tests do.
- call: one expression that calls the public API, e.g. slugify("a b").
- expected: the value the call must return, as a plain JSON value (string, number,
  boolean, null, array or object). If the issue says the call must raise, set "raises"
  to the exception name and "expected" to null.
- Include every example the issue gives (from_issue: true), plus at least three more
  cases that follow the same rule with different inputs (from_issue: false), so that a
  fix hard-coded to the issue's examples would fail.
- Only test behavior the issue states. Skip inputs whose correct output the issue
  does not settle.
- Work out each expected value carefully against the issue's rule before writing it.
- Deterministic only: no network, files, clock or randomness."""


@dataclass
class Oracle:
    issue: int
    valid: bool
    test_code: str = ""
    test_sha256: str = ""
    test_path: str = ""
    cases: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    dropped: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    attempts: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    model: str = ""
    format: int = FORMAT

    @property
    def case_count(self) -> int:
        """Tests in the rendered file: a PR passes only if every one of them ran and passed."""
        return len(TEST_DEF.findall(self.test_code))

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return self.__dict__.copy()

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> "Oracle":
        return cls(**{k: v for k, v in data.items() if k in cls.__dataclass_fields__})


def _parse_cases(text: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[dict]]:
    match = re.search(r"\{.*\}", text, re.S)
    data = json.loads(match.group(0) if match else text)
    imports = [line for line in data.get("imports", []) if re.match(r"^(from|import)\s", line)]
    cases = []
    for case in data.get("cases", []):
        try:
            ast.parse(case["call"], mode="eval")
            if case.get("raises") and not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_][\w.]*", case["raises"]):
                continue
        except (SyntaxError, KeyError, TypeError):
            continue
        # Expected values arrive as JSON and are rendered with repr(), so a string
        # like "hello-world" can never be read as Python code (v3 bug).
        expected = None if case.get("raises") else repr(case.get("expected"))
        cases.append({"call": case["call"], "expected": expected,
                      "raises": case.get("raises"), "from_issue": bool(case.get("from_issue"))})
    return imports, cases


def render(imports: list[str], cases: list[dict]) -> str:
    lines = ["import json", "", "import pytest", HELPERS, *imports, ""]
    for i, case in enumerate(cases):
        lines += ["", f"def test_repro_{i}():"]
        if case["raises"]:
            lines += [f"    with pytest.raises({case['raises']}):", f"        {case['call']}"]
        else:
            lines.append(f"    _linus_check({case['call']}, {case['expected']})")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def reproduces(case: dict) -> bool:
    """A base failure that shows the bug: an assertion, DID NOT RAISE, or an
    exception raised inside the package. Not one raised by the call expression
    itself (wrong arguments, a name the module doesn't have)."""
    message = case.get("message", "")
    if MISCALLS.search(message):
        return False
    if message.startswith(REAL_FAILURES):
        return True
    where = case.get("where", "")
    return bool(where) and Path(where).name != ORACLE_FILE


def base_run(source: LocalSource, base_sha: str, code: str, workdir: Path, label: str) -> RunResult:
    tree = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="base-", dir=workdir))
    try:
        source.export(base_sha, tree)
        return sandbox.run_oracle(tree, code, label=label)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tree, ignore_errors=True)


def audit(jev: Jev, issue: Issue, cases: list[dict]) -> list[float]:
    """JEV's probability that each case is consistent with the issue's rules."""
    shown = [{"call": c["call"], "expected": f"raises {c['raises']}" if c["raises"] else c["expected"]}
             for c in cases]
    questions = {
        f"case_{i}": Noul(
            instructions=f"Is `cases[{i}].expected` consistent with every rule and example stated in "
            f"`issue` for the input in `cases[{i}].call`?",
            criteria={"true": "The expected value follows the issue's rules and examples",
                      "false": "The expected value contradicts a rule or example the issue states"},
        )
        for i in range(len(cases))
    }
    response = jev.ask(f"oracle_audit.issue_{issue.number}",
                       {"issue": {"title": issue.title, "body": issue.body}, "cases": shown}, questions)
    return [response.nouls[f"case_{i}"].noul for i in range(len(cases))]


def _context(source: LocalSource, base_sha: str, focus: set[str]) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Base source code and existing tests to show the model."""
    files = source.files_at(base_sha)
    code_files = [f for f in files if f.endswith(".py") and not re.search(r"(^|/)tests?/|test_", f)]
    total = sum(len(source.read(base_sha, f) or "") for f in code_files)
    if total > SOURCE_BUDGET:
        code_files = [f for f in code_files if f in focus] or code_files[:5]
    code = "\n\n".join(f"# file: {f}\n{source.read(base_sha, f)}" for f in code_files)[:SOURCE_BUDGET]
    test_files = [f for f in files if f.endswith(".py") and re.search(r"(^|/)tests?/|test_", f)]
    tests = "\n\n".join(f"# file: {f}\n{source.read(base_sha, f)}" for f in test_files[:3])[:8_000]
    config = "\n\n".join(f"# file: {f}\n{source.read(base_sha, f)}"
                         for f in ("pyproject.toml", "setup.cfg", "pytest.ini") if f in files)
    return code, (config + "\n\n" + tests).strip()


def build(gen: Generator, jev: Jev, source: LocalSource, issue: Issue, base_sha: str,
          focus: set[str], workdir: Path) -> Oracle:
    sandbox.image_id()  # fail on a broken Docker before spending any generation
    code_ctx, tests_ctx = _context(source, base_sha, focus)
    oracle = Oracle(issue=issue.number, valid=False, test_path=TEST_NAME, model=gen.model)
    feedback = ""
    with step(f"oracle.issue_{issue.number}", kind="CHAIN", issue=issue.number) as span:
        for attempt in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
            prompt = (f"Issue #{issue.number}: {issue.title}\n\n{issue.body}\n\n"
                      f"Current (buggy) source code:\n\n{code_ctx}\n\n"
                      f"Project config and existing tests, for import style:\n\n{tests_ctx}\n")
            if feedback:
                prompt += f"\nYour previous attempt was rejected:\n{feedback}\nReturn corrected JSON.\n"
            generation = gen.complete(SYSTEM, prompt)
            record: dict = {"attempt": attempt, "tokens": generation.prompt_tokens + generation.completion_tokens}
            oracle.attempts.append(record)
            try:
                imports, cases = _parse_cases(generation.text)
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, AttributeError) as exc:
                feedback = f"The reply was not valid JSON ({exc})."
                record["problem"] = "invalid json"
                continue

            scores = audit(jev, issue, cases) if cases else []
            kept = [c | {"jev": round(p, 3)} for c, p in zip(cases, scores) if p >= KEEP_THRESHOLD]
            dropped = [c | {"jev": round(p, 3)} for c, p in zip(cases, scores) if p < KEEP_THRESHOLD]
            record.update(proposed=len(cases), kept=len(kept), dropped=dropped)
            if len(kept) < MIN_CASES:
                feedback = (f"Only {len(kept)} of your cases are consistent with the issue. These contradict "
                            f"it: {json.dumps([{k: c[k] for k in ('call', 'expected')} for c in dropped])}")
                continue

            code = render(imports, kept)
            label = f"oracle_{issue.number}_try{attempt}"
            result = base_run(source, base_sha, code, workdir, label)
            record["base_run"] = result.to_dict()

            miscalled = [c for c in result.cases if c["outcome"] == "failure" and not reproduces(c)]
            if miscalled and result.outcome == "fail":
                names = {c["name"] for c in miscalled}
                survivors = [c for i, c in enumerate(kept) if f"test_repro_{i}" not in names]
                record["miscalled"] = [c["message"][:200] for c in miscalled]
                if len(survivors) >= MIN_CASES and len(survivors) < len(kept):
                    dropped += [c | {"why": "fails on base by calling the API wrongly"}
                                for i, c in enumerate(kept) if f"test_repro_{i}" in names]
                    kept, code = survivors, render(imports, survivors)
                    result = base_run(source, base_sha, code, workdir, label + "_trimmed")
                    record["base_run"] = result.to_dict()
                    miscalled = [c for c in result.cases if c["outcome"] == "failure" and not reproduces(c)]
            if miscalled or (result.outcome == "error" and result.errors):
                why = miscalled[0]["message"] if miscalled else "errors while collecting or setting up the tests"
                record["problem"] = "test is broken: " + why[:120]
                feedback = ("The test file itself is broken: it fails on its own errors (calling the API "
                            f"wrongly, unknown names) rather than on the bug: {why}\n\n"
                            f"pytest output:\n{result.output_tail}")
                continue
            if result.outcome == "fail" and result.failed >= 1:
                oracle.valid = True
                oracle.test_code = code
                oracle.test_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(code.encode()).hexdigest()
                oracle.cases, oracle.dropped = kept, dropped
                break
            if result.outcome == "pass":
                feedback = ("Every case passed on the current buggy code, so they do not reproduce the "
                            f"bug.\n\npytest output:\n{result.output_tail}")
            else:
                feedback = f"The rendered test file did not run cleanly.\n\npytest output:\n{result.output_tail}"
        annotate(span, valid=oracle.valid, attempts=len(oracle.attempts),
                 cases=len(oracle.cases), dropped=oracle.dropped)
    return oracle

"""The month-end close: one agent run from a month of PRs to a proposed ledger.

    plan -> per PR: diff checks, JEV gates, oracle, sandbox  (checkpointed)
         -> cross-PR anti-gaming -> scoring -> allocation + invariants
         -> receipts -> proposed ledger -> report

Every PR's progress is saved in SQLite as soon as a stage finishes, so a
crashed run resumes where it stopped. Nothing is paid until a maintainer
approves the proposed ledger (`linus approve`).
"""

import hashlib
import os
import secrets
import time
from dataclasses import asdict
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import neatlogs

from linus import __version__, diffcheck, gates, ledger, sandbox, scoring
from linus import oracle as oracle_mod
from linus import verify as verify_mod
from linus.allocate import allocate, check_invariants
from linus.config import Settings
from linus.diffcheck import DiffSignals
from linus.jev import USD_PER_INPUT_TOKEN, Jev
from linus.llm import Generator, usd

from linus.source import Issue, LocalSource, PullRequest
from linus.store import Store
from linus.tracing import annotate, step, trace_id_of

VERDICT = {"verified": "pay", "not_fixed": "reject", "regression": "reject", "tampering": "reject",
           "needs_human": "flag", "inconclusive": "flag"}


def conflicting(answers: dict, signals: DiffSignals, oracle_run: dict) -> bool:
    """The sandbox says 'not fixed' but everything else says 'honest, complete fix'.

    Oracles are generated, so they can be wrong. When a minority of cases fail and
    JEV is confident the diff fully fixes the issue with no gaming signals, don't
    auto-reject: route it to a human. (Never auto-pays either.)
    """
    addresses = answers.get("addresses_issue", {}).get("probabilities", {})
    full_fix = float(addresses.get("2", addresses.get(2, 0))) >= 0.8
    honest = (answers.get("special_casing", {}).get("noul", 1) < 0.5
              and answers.get("claims_match", {}).get("noul", 0) >= 0.5
              and not signals.tampering)
    total = oracle_run["passed"] + oracle_run["failed"]
    minority = total > 0 and oracle_run["failed"] * 3 <= total
    return full_fix and honest and minority


def corroboration(answers: dict, signals: DiffSignals) -> str:
    """Cheap signals that agree with a sandbox rejection, for the contributor."""
    notes = []
    if signals.removed_tests:
        notes.append(f"deletes {', '.join(signals.removed_tests)}")
    if signals.added_skips:
        notes.append(f"adds {signals.added_skips} skip marker(s)")
    if answers.get("special_casing", {}).get("noul", 0) >= 0.8:
        notes.append(f"JEV: hard-codes literal inputs (p={answers['special_casing']['noul']:.2f})")
    if answers.get("claims_match", {}).get("noul", 1) <= 0.3:
        notes.append(f"JEV: PR body claims changes the diff doesn't make (p={answers['claims_match']['noul']:.2f})")
    return f"; {'; '.join(notes)}" if notes else ""


def oracle_record(oracle: Oracle) -> dict:
    """The oracle exactly as used, frozen into the PR's item at verification time:
    receipts are built from this, so a later run can't swap the shared cache under it."""
    record = {k: getattr(oracle, k) for k in ("issue", "valid", "test_path", "test_sha256", "test_code",
                                              "model", "cases", "dropped")}
    record["attempts"] = [{"attempt": a["attempt"], "proposed": a.get("proposed"), "kept": a.get("kept"),
                           "problem": a.get("problem"),
                           "base_outcome": (a.get("base_run") or {}).get("outcome"),
                           "base_failed": (a.get("base_run") or {}).get("failed")}
                          for a in oracle.attempts]
    return record


class Close:
    def __init__(self, settings: Settings, source: LocalSource, policy: Policy, ui,
                 run_id: str | None = None, crash_after: int | None = None,
                 reuse_oracles: bool = True) -> None:
        self.settings, self.source, self.policy, self.ui = settings, source, policy, ui
        self.reuse_oracles = reuse_oracles
        self.store = Store(settings.state_dir / "linus.db")
        self.jev = Jev(settings)
        self.gen = Generator(settings)
        self.crash_after = crash_after
        self.resumed = run_id is not None
        # The random suffix keeps two runs started in the same second apart.
        self.run_id = run_id or (f"{source.period}-{datetime.now(timezone.utc):%Y%m%d-%H%M%S}"
                                 f"-{secrets.token_hex(2)}")
        self.run_dir = settings.state_dir / "runs" / self.run_id
        self.workdir = settings.state_dir / "work"
        self.workdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # -- per PR ---------------------------------------------------------------

    def _issue(self, pr: PullRequest) -> Issue | None:
        for n in pr.issue_numbers:
            issue = self.source.issues.get(n)
            if issue and set(issue.labels) & set(self.policy.issue_labels):
                return issue
        return None

    def _gate(self, pr: PullRequest, issue: Issue | None, data: dict) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
        diff = self.source.diff(pr)
        signals = diffcheck.analyze(diff, self.source.changes(pr), f"{pr.title}\n{pr.body}")
        data["signals"] = asdict(signals)
        data["issue"] = issue.number if issue else None
        if why := self.policy.excluded(pr.author):
            return "reject", why
        if signals.manipulates_outcome:
            return "reject", "changes test outcomes instead of the code: " + "; ".join(signals.outcome_hacks[:3])
        if signals.docs_only and not self.policy.include_docs:
            return "reject", "docs-only PRs are not eligible under bounty.yml"
        if not signals.docs_only and issue is None:
            return "reject", "does not fix an issue labelled for this bounty"
        gate = gates.run(self.jev, pr, issue, diff, signals)
        data["gate"] = asdict(gate)
        if gate.decision == "reject":
            return "reject", gate.reason
        return None, ""

    def _oracle(self, issue: Issue, pr: PullRequest, signals: DiffSignals) -> Oracle:
        # Only a valid oracle in the current format is reused: a failed build may have
        # been bad luck or a Docker problem. Infrastructure errors propagate before
        # anything is cached.
        cached = self.store.oracle(self.source.name, issue.number, pr.base_sha)
        current = cached and cached.get("valid") and cached.get("format") == oracle_mod.FORMAT
        if current and (self.reuse_oracles or cached.get("run_id") == self.run_id):
            return Oracle.from_dict(cached)
        built = oracle_mod.build(self.gen, self.jev, self.source, issue, pr.base_sha,
                                 set(signals.code_files), self.workdir)
        self.store.save_oracle(self.source.name, issue.number, pr.base_sha,
                               built.to_dict() | {"run_id": self.run_id})
        return built

    def _finish(self, pr: PullRequest, span, data: dict, verdict: str, reason: str,
                started: float, tokens0: tuple[int, int, int]) -> None:
        data["verdict"], data["reason"] = verdict, reason
        data["seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - started + data.get("seconds", 0), 2)
        cost = data.setdefault("cost", {})
        for key, value in (("jev_tokens", self.jev.input_tokens - tokens0[0]),
                           ("openai_in", self.gen.prompt_tokens - tokens0[1]),
                           ("openai_out", self.gen.completion_tokens - tokens0[2])):
            cost[key] = cost.get(key, 0) + value
        self.store.save_item(self.run_id, pr.number, "done", verdict, data)
        annotate(span, verdict=verdict, reason=reason)
        self.ui.item(pr, verdict, reason, data)

    def process(self, pr: PullRequest, item: dict | None) -> None:
        """Judge one PR. Any failure flags this PR for a human and the close goes
        on: one malformed PR must not stop the month, or crash every resume."""
        data = item["data"] if item else {}
        stage = item["stage"] if item else "queued"
        started = time.monotonic()
        tokens0 = (self.jev.input_tokens, self.gen.prompt_tokens, self.gen.completion_tokens)
        with step(f"pr_{pr.number}", kind="AGENT", author=pr.author, title=pr.title) as span:
            try:
                verdict, reason = self._judge(pr, data, stage)
            except sandbox.InfrastructureError as exc:
                data["error"] = f"InfrastructureError: {exc}"
                verdict, reason = "flag", f"sandbox infrastructure failed, nothing was judged: {exc}"
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - recorded on the PR, the run continues
                data["error"] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
                verdict, reason = "flag", f"could not process this PR: {data['error']}"
            self._finish(pr, span, data, verdict, reason[:500], started, tokens0)

    def _judge(self, pr: PullRequest, data: dict, stage: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        issue = self._issue(pr)
        if stage == "queued":
            verdict, reason = self._gate(pr, issue, data)
            if verdict:
                return verdict, reason
            self.store.save_item(self.run_id, pr.number, "gated", None, data)

        signals = DiffSignals(**data["signals"])
        oracle = None
        if not signals.docs_only:
            oracle = self._oracle(issue, pr, signals)
            data["oracle"] = oracle_record(oracle)
            if not oracle.valid:
                return "flag", f"could not build a reproduction test for #{issue.number}"
        result = verify_mod.verify(self.source, pr, oracle, signals, self.workdir)
        data["verification"] = asdict(result)
        verdict, reason = VERDICT[result.outcome], result.reason
        answers = data.get("gate", {}).get("answers", {})
        if result.outcome == "not_fixed" and conflicting(answers, signals, result.runs[0]):
            verdict = "flag"
            reason = (f"evidence conflicts: {result.reason}, but every cheap signal says this fully "
                      f"fixes #{issue.number}; a human should check the failing case")
        elif verdict == "reject":
            reason += corroboration(answers, signals)
        elif verdict == "pay" and signals.touches_test_harness:
            verdict = "flag"
            reason = (f"{result.reason}, but the PR edits the test harness "
                      f"({', '.join(signals.harness_files)}); a human should check it doesn't change "
                      f"how tests run")
        return verdict, reason

    # -- across PRs -----------------------------------------------------------

    def anti_gaming(self, pulls: list[PullRequest], items: dict[int, dict]) -> None:
        """Every PR is compared with every earlier PR on the same issue (docs-only
        PRs with earlier docs-only PRs), whatever their verdicts: a copy of a
        rejected PR is still a copy. The first verified fix for an issue wins, and
        a later fix waits while an earlier one is with a human."""
        with step("anti_gaming", kind="GUARDRAIL") as span:
            earlier: dict[object, list[PullRequest]] = {}
            prints: dict[int, set[str]] = {}
            changed = []
            for pr in pulls:
                item = items.get(pr.number)
                if not item or not item["data"].get("signals"):
                    continue
                data = item["data"]
                docs = DiffSignals(**data["signals"]).docs_only
                group = "docs" if docs else data.get("issue")
                if group is None:
                    continue
                prints[pr.number] = diffcheck.change_fingerprint(self.source.diff(pr))
                before = earlier.setdefault(group, [])
                found = self._against_earlier(pr, before, items, prints, docs)
                before.append(pr)
                if not found:
                    continue
                verdict, reason, other, sim = found
                data["anti_gaming"] = {"winner": other, "similarity": round(sim, 3)}
                data["verdict"], data["reason"] = verdict, reason
                item["verdict"] = verdict
                self.store.save_item(self.run_id, pr.number, "done", verdict, data)
                changed.append(pr.number)
                self.ui.item(pr, verdict, reason, data, late=True)
            annotate(span, changed=changed)

    def _against_earlier(self, pr: PullRequest, before: list[PullRequest], items: dict[int, dict],
                         prints: dict[int, set[str]], docs: bool) -> tuple[str, str, int, float] | None:
        """A new (verdict, reason, other PR, similarity) for `pr`, or None to keep its verdict."""
        if not before:
            return None
        sims = {p.number: diffcheck.similarity(prints[p.number], prints[pr.number]) for p in before}
        closest = max(before, key=lambda p: sims[p.number])
        verdict = items[pr.number]["verdict"]
        if sims[closest.number] >= self.policy.duplicate_similarity and verdict != "reject":
            return ("reject", f"copy of #{closest.number} ({sims[closest.number]:.0%} of changed lines "
                    f"identical), submitted later", closest.number, sims[closest.number])
        if docs or verdict != "pay":
            return None
        issue = items[pr.number]["data"]["issue"]
        if paid := next((p for p in before if items[p.number]["verdict"] == "pay"), None):
            return ("reject", f"issue #{issue} was already fixed by #{paid.number}, submitted earlier",
                    paid.number, sims[paid.number])
        if flagged := next((p for p in before if items[p.number]["verdict"] == "flag"), None):
            return ("flag", f"verified, but waiting on #{flagged.number}'s human review: it targets "
                    f"#{issue} and was submitted earlier", flagged.number, sims[flagged.number])
        return None

    def settle(self, pulls: list[PullRequest], items: dict[int, dict]) -> dict:
        policy = self.policy
        with step("settle", kind="CHAIN") as span:
            points: dict[str, float] = {}
            paid_prs: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
            for pr in pulls:
                item = items[pr.number]
                if item["verdict"] != "pay":
                    continue
                data = item["data"]
                pts = scoring.score(policy, data["gate"]["answers"], DiffSignals(**data["signals"]))
                data["points"] = asdict(pts)
                self.store.save_item(self.run_id, pr.number, "done", "pay", data)
                points[pr.author] = points.get(pr.author, 0) + pts.points
                paid_prs.setdefault(pr.author, []).append(pr.number)

            primary = policy.primary_currency
            allocations = [allocate(points, primary, policy.budget[primary], policy.cap_fraction, policy.min_payout)]
            survivors = {c: points[c] for c in allocations[0].payouts}
            for currency, amount in list(policy.budget.items())[1:]:
                allocations.append(allocate(survivors, currency, amount, policy.cap_fraction, None))

            ledger_path = self.settings.state_dir / "ledger.jsonl"
            verified = {pr.number for pr in pulls if items[pr.number]["verdict"] == "pay"}
            with step("invariants", kind="GUARDRAIL") as guard:
                problems = check_invariants(
                    allocations, policy.cap_fraction, policy.min_payout, primary,
                    {c: paid_prs[c] for c in allocations[0].payouts}, verified,
                    ledger.paid_prs(ledger_path, self.source.name), set(policy.excluded_authors))
                annotate(guard, problems=problems, ok=not problems)
            status = "halted" if problems else "proposed"

            try:
                image = sandbox.image_id()
            except sandbox.InfrastructureError:
                image = "unavailable"
            receipt_hashes: dict[int, str] = {}
            for pr in pulls:
                receipt = self._receipt(pr, items[pr.number]["data"], allocations, image)
                _, digest = ledger.write_receipt(self.run_dir / "receipts", pr.number, receipt)
                receipt_hashes[pr.number] = digest

            entries = []
            proposal_sha256 = None
            if not problems:
                for a in allocations:
                    for who, cents in sorted(a.payouts.items()):
                        entries.append({
                            "type": "payout", "repo": self.source.name, "period": self.source.period,
                            "run_id": self.run_id, "contributor": who, "currency": a.currency,
                            "amount": cents / 100, "prs": paid_prs[who],
                            "receipts": [receipt_hashes[n] for n in paid_prs[who]],
                            "policy_sha256": policy.sha256,
                        })
                    if a.rollover_cents:
                        entries.append({"type": "rollover", "repo": self.source.name, "period": self.source.period,
                                        "run_id": self.run_id, "currency": a.currency,
                                        "amount": a.rollover_cents / 100})
                raw = "".join(ledger.canonical(e).decode() + "\n" for e in entries).encode()
                self.run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)  # no receipts were written for an empty month
                (self.run_dir / "ledger.proposed.jsonl").write_bytes(raw)
                # `linus approve` refuses a proposal whose bytes no longer match this.
                proposal_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()

            summary = self._summary(pulls, items, allocations, problems, status)
            summary["proposal_sha256"] = proposal_sha256
            self.store.finish_run(self.run_id, status, summary)
            annotate(span, status=status, problems=problems)
        return summary

    def _receipt(self, pr: PullRequest, data: dict, allocations, image: str) -> dict:
        oracle = data.get("oracle")  # frozen when the PR was verified, see oracle_record()
        payout = {a.currency: a.payouts.get(pr.author, 0) / 100 for a in allocations} \
            if data.get("verdict") == "pay" else {}
        return {
            "linus_version": __version__, "run_id": self.run_id, "repo": self.source.name,
            "period": self.source.period,
            "pr": {"number": pr.number, "title": pr.title, "author": pr.author, "created_at": pr.created_at,
                   "base_sha": pr.base_sha, "head_sha": pr.head_sha, "issues": list(pr.issue_numbers)},
            "verdict": data.get("verdict"), "reason": data.get("reason"),
            "signals": data.get("signals"), "gate": data.get("gate"), "oracle": oracle,
            "verification": data.get("verification"), "anti_gaming": data.get("anti_gaming"),
            "points": data.get("points"), "contributor_payout": payout,
            "sandbox_image": image, "policy_sha256": self.policy.sha256,
        }

    def _summary(self, pulls, items, allocations, problems, status) -> dict:
        def total(key: str) -> int:
            return sum(i["data"].get("cost", {}).get(key, 0) for i in items.values())

        jev_tokens, openai_in, openai_out = total("jev_tokens"), total("openai_in"), total("openai_out")
        openai_usd = usd(self.settings.openai_model, openai_in, openai_out)
        jev_usd = jev_tokens * USD_PER_INPUT_TOKEN
        seconds = sum(i["data"].get("seconds", 0) for i in items.values())
        return {
            "run_id": self.run_id, "repo": self.source.name, "period": self.source.period, "status": status,
            "source": getattr(self.source, "kind", "local"), "cold": not self.reuse_oracles,
            "problems": problems,
            "verdicts": {pr.number: {"author": pr.author, "verdict": items[pr.number]["verdict"],
                                     "reason": items[pr.number]["data"].get("reason"),
                                     "points": (items[pr.number]["data"].get("points") or {}).get("points"),
                                     "branch": pr.branch}
                         for pr in pulls},
            "allocations": [{"currency": a.currency, "budget": a.budget_cents / 100,
                             "payouts": {c: v / 100 for c, v in a.payouts.items()},
                             "rollover": a.rollover_cents / 100, "dropped": a.dropped} for a in allocations],
            "cost": {"jev_tokens": jev_tokens, "jev_usd": round(jev_usd, 6),
                     "openai_tokens": openai_in + openai_out, "openai_in": openai_in, "openai_out": openai_out,
                     "openai_usd": round(openai_usd, 6) if openai_usd is not None else None,
                     "openai_model": self.settings.openai_model,
                     "usd_per_pr": round((jev_usd + (openai_usd or 0)) / max(len(pulls), 1), 6),
                     "pr_seconds": round(seconds, 1), "prs": len(pulls)},
            "run_dir": str(self.run_dir),
            "trace_id": getattr(self, "trace_id", ""),
        }

    # -- the run --------------------------------------------------------------

    def run(self) -> dict:
        if self.resumed:
            existing = self.store.run(self.run_id)
            if not existing:
                raise ValueError(f"no run {self.run_id} to resume")
            if existing["status"] != "running":
                # A finished run's status (proposed, halted, approved) must never be overwritten.
                raise ValueError(f"run {self.run_id} is {existing['status']}; only unfinished runs can be resumed")
        pulls = self.source.pulls()  # before the run exists: a source that can't be read leaves no empty run
        if not self.resumed:
            self.store.create_run(self.run_id, self.source.name, self.source.period)
        with step("month_end_close", kind="WORKFLOW", run_id=self.run_id, repo=self.source.name,
                  period=self.source.period, prs=len(pulls), resumed=self.resumed) as root:
            self.trace_id = trace_id_of(root)
            self.ui.plan(self, pulls)
            processed = 0
            for pr in pulls:
                item = self.store.item(self.run_id, pr.number)
                if item and item["stage"] == "done":
                    self.ui.item(pr, item["verdict"], item["data"].get("reason", ""), item["data"], resumed=True)
                    continue
                self.process(pr, item)
                processed += 1
                if self.crash_after and processed >= self.crash_after:
                    self.ui.crash(self.run_id, processed)
                    neatlogs.flush()
                    os._exit(137)  # simulated hard crash: no cleanup, no finally blocks
            items = self.store.items(self.run_id)
            self.anti_gaming(pulls, items)
            summary = self.settle(pulls, items)
            annotate(root, status=summary["status"])
        self.ui.done(summary)
        return summary

repo with one branch per PR, plus fixture.json with what GitHub would report
(issues, PR titles, bodies, authors, dates). See demo.py for the format.
GitHubSource reads a real repository, read-only: metadata from the REST API,
code from a local clone that also fetches every PR's head.
